transcript.text: Hi, my Hotpoint Aquarius dryer is taking forever to dry and the top gets really hot. Model is TCM580GUK if that helps

For the Hotpoint Aquarius TCM580GUK (a condenser tumble dryer), slow drying plus a very hot top is most often caused by restricted airflow or a blocked condenser/filter system.

### First: stop using it if
• There’s a burning/plastic smell, smoke, buzzing, or the casing is too hot to comfortably touch.
• Clothes come out unusually hot or damp after a full cycle.
• It keeps stopping or shows warning lights.

Switch it off and unplug it before cleaning anything.

### Things to check/clean

1. Clean the fluff/lint filter
• Usually inside the door opening.
• Remove all fluff after every load.
• If it looks clean but feels coated, wash it in warm water with a little washing-up liquid, rinse and let it dry completely. Fabric-softener residue can block airflow.

2. Clean the condenser unit
• On this style of dryer it is normally behind the lower front flap.
• Remove it carefully and rinse fluff from the fins with a gentle flow of warm water, from both sides if possible.
• Do not use sharp tools, brushes with hard bristles, or bend the thin fins.
• Let excess water drain before refitting it securely.
• Also vacuum/wipe loose fluff from the condenser compartment and door seal area.

3. Empty the water container
• A full tank can affect operation on condenser dryers.
• Empty it after each use and make sure it is pushed fully back in.

4. Avoid overloading
• A packed drum takes dramatically longer to dry. Try a half-load of towels or mixed laundry as a test.
• Make sure items were well spun in the washing machine first; ideally 1000–1400 rpm.

5. Room temperature / placement
• Condenser dryers work poorly in a very cold utility room, garage or unheated space.
• Leave space around the dryer and don’t cover the top or block any vents.

### About the hot top
The top of a condenser dryer can get noticeably warm in normal use, but it should not become painfully hot, smell hot, or make the room excessively steamy. If cleaning the filter and condenser does not improve drying, likely causes include a failing fan, blocked internal ducting, faulty temperature sensor/thermostat, or condenser/pump issue. Those need an appliance engineer rather than further dismantling.

If you tell me whether it is still producing heat, whether the water tank fills, and whether any lights are flashing, I can narrow it down further.

Thank you, that's helpful. It is still producing heat, the drum turns normally and water does collect in the container (it was about half full and empties fine). No lights are flashing, and the 'empty water' and 'clean condenser' lights aren't lit. The top panel does feel very hot to the touch though, and I'm afraid I do sometimes forget to clean the fluff filter.

That combination strongly points to reduced airflow from lint build-up rather than a water-pump fault: it is heating, tumbling and collecting water, but cannot move air efficiently through the laundry and condenser. That makes drying take much longer and can make the top/cabinet hotter than normal.

### What I’d do before using it again
1. Switch it off, unplug it, and let it cool fully.
2. Clean the fluff filter thoroughly — not just the visible layer.
• Remove the filter from the door area.
• Peel/vacuum away all lint.
• If it has a grey, waxy-looking film, wash it in warm water with a tiny amount of washing-up liquid, rinse thoroughly and allow it to dry completely before refitting. Fabric-softener and detergent residue can block it even when it looks fairly clean.
3. Clean the condenser behind the lower front flap.
• Remove it as instructed on the flap/manual.
• Rinse it through gently with warm water until the water runs clear.
• Clear lint from the condenser housing/door seals as far as you can reach without poking tools inside or damaging the fins.
• Refit it properly and make sure the flap is closed securely.
4. Empty the water container and check it seats fully.

Then try a small, well-spun load rather than a full drum. It should be distinctly improved after one normal drying cycle.

### When to stop and arrange repair
Do not keep using it if, after cleaning, the top is still too hot to leave your hand on comfortably, drying remains very slow, or there is any hot/burning smell. Internal lint can build up around the fan/heater or air channels, and a restricted fan or failing thermostat can cause overheating even if no warning lights appear. That needs an appliance engineer rather than further dismantling at home.

For future use, clean the door filter after every load. On a condenser dryer, that one habit makes a major difference to drying time, electricity use and overheating risk.
